header.userPrompt:
Improve the PR titles and descriptions that Orca's flows generate. Today they are wordy and sometimes state things that aren't true. Example: a recent generated description claimed a check would catch problems on "macOS CI", which doesn't exist in the repo — the summariser invented it.

Two causes, two changes:

## 1. Rewrite the summariser prompt

File: `flow/src/main/resources/orca/pr/prompts/summarise.md` (loaded as `PrPrompts.Summarise`, used by `summarisePr` in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/pr/summarisePr.scala`). Keep the existing `Closes #N` rules (and leave `closing-refs.md` alone unless it conflicts). Replace the "a few short paragraphs covering what changed and why" guidance with rules along these lines:

- Title: one line, imperative, says what the PR does.
- Body: as short as possible — one to three short paragraphs, or a short bullet list when there are several separate changes. Plain, simple language; don't try to sound smart.
- Say what changed, why (only as stated in the context), and anything a reviewer must know that the diff doesn't make obvious.
- State only facts visible in the diff or given in the context. Never guess or invent claims about CI, platforms, environments, performance, motivation, testing done, or consequences.
- Don't restate what the code obviously does line by line, and don't list every file touched.
- No filler or marketing phrasing ("This change improves…", "This ensures…", "robust", "seamless").

Keep the prompt itself short and direct.

## 2. Use the full coding agent, not the cheap tier, as the PR summariser

The cheap tier (e.g. Haiku) is the model that invented facts. Switch the summariser from `codingAgent.cheap` to `codingAgent` in:
- `flows/simple.sc`, `flows/implement.sc`, `flows/implement-enhanced.sc`, `flows/implement-interactive.sc`, `flows/issue-pr.sc` (the `summarisingAgent = codingAgent.cheap` argument to `openPrIfGitHub`/`openPrFromBranch`);
- `flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc`: only in `prSummary` (`summarisePr(agent = codingAgent.cheap, ...)`). Leave the `codingAgent.cheap.run(...)` in `confirmReproductionMatches` as is.
- Docs/examples that show the summariser: `README.md` (the `openPrIfGitHub(summarisingAgent = codingAgent.cheap, ...)` line), `docs/authoring/pull-requests.md`, `docs/authoring/tutorial.md`. Keep them consistent with the flows.
- `summarisePr`'s scaladoc says "Use a cheap model." — update it so it no longer recommends the cheap tier (one short sentence at most, or drop it).

Don't change any other `.cheap` usage (branch naming, review picker, lint, etc.). Don't touch `docs/plans/`, `docs/research/` or `docs/superpowers/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `sbt test` passes (including `runner/src/test/scala/flowtests/FlowCompilesTest.scala` and the `flow` module's PR tests); fix any test that asserts on the old prompt wording.
- Built-in flows still compile (the CI `flow-scripts` job runs `sbt publishLocal "shell/testOnly *BuiltInFlowsCompileTest"`).
- No new compiler warnings; `sbt scalafmtCheckAll` clean.
- PR description: short, plain, only facts from this change.
